name: The Sixfold Snowflake

detectability.signature: Hexagonally modulated subspace shriek detectable at eighteen million kilometers

proximity: Angle-measuring instruments disagree by growing margins
Starfield distortions fold inward against the direction of travel
Crews report headaches and the sense of being watched from six sides
contact: Interior geometry inverts; straight approaches arrive curved
Ships observe their own hulls through internal sightlines that cannot exist
Instrument suites return six mutually exclusive positions at once
prolonged_exposure: Progressive reality breakdown of vessel architecture
Consciousness transfer between crew members and their six-sided echoes

phenomena: Impossible geometries visible within the frosted boundary
Visible distortion of the starfield into sixfold motifs
Objects appearing larger and smaller than measurement allows
Subspace interference patterns repeating with hexagonal symmetry
hazards: Reality breakdown within the inverted interior
Dimensional displacement with no consistent exit
Loss of crew identity to the zone's echoing structure
opportunities: Communication attempts with adjacent geometries of existence
Ultimate proving ground for exotic theories of space
known_incidents: 2253 - Lost colony ship Meridian Child returned crewed and intact after ninety years away
2289 - Expedition Torvast entered with nine; three returned refusing to describe the interior
description: From a distance the Sixfold Snowflake looks almost gentle: a sphere of frosted starlight whose surface repeats a hexagonal pattern no two survey photographs agree upon. Closer in, the pattern resolves into corridors of geometry branching six directions at once, and the eye begins to ache before the mind understands why. Nothing about its outline holds still longer than an instrument's integration time.

Inside, straight lines arrive where curves were aimed, parallel courses meet, and a ship's bow can be glimpsed through her own stern ports. The zone's volatility is absolute; volleys of angle-inversion arrive without rhythm, and no two entries have ever produced matching deck logs. Crews who linger report seeing themselves at neighboring portholes, waving with a delay that is not quite a reflection's.

The zone announced itself in 2253 by returning the lost colony ship Meridian Child ninety years after her disappearance, crewed, intact, and insisting she had been gone only an afternoon. Every expedition since has come back less intact than the last. Xenometricians cite it as the sector's premier argument that space is a local custom rather than a law.

Buoy chains mark the boundary at eighteen million kilometers' respectful distance, and underwriters refuse coverage inside them. Three research consortiums keep permanent watch rotations, ostensibly studying the zone and quietly hoping it keeps to its own weather. No crew has ever entered it twice on purpose, and it has never once refused anyone who insisted.
